title: Clients Not Getting IPs From Central DHCP Server
symptoms: Users on a new VLAN cannot obtain IP addresses
The DHCP server is on a different subnet and works for other VLANs
The router interface for the new VLAN is up/up
rootCause: The DHCP relay agent (ip helper-address) was not configured on the new VLAN's router interface. Without it, DHCP broadcasts from clients are not forwarded to the central server on another subnet.

steps.prompt: Which command shows the IP addresses assigned to clients by the DHCP server?
steps.hint: If clients from this VLAN are missing, the server never received their requests.

steps.prompt: Which command shows the router interface configuration to check for ip helper-address?
steps.hint: Look for 'ip helper-address X.X.X.X' pointing at your DHCP server.

steps.prompt: Which command shows DHCP relay statistics on the router?
steps.hint: Counters here confirm whether relay is even seeing client requests.
